children: Phillips Edison is expanding its joint venture with Northwestern Mutual to acquire a $377.5 million portfolio of 13 shopping centers.

The joint venture, called Grocery Retail Partners I, will acquire the portfolio from Phillips Edison. The venture's term was also extended by a decade to 2036. Phillips Edison will retain a roughly 14% interest in the venture, while Northwestern Mutual's stake will be around 86%.

"In addition to the durable fee revenue generated, this expanded joint venture advances PECO's capital allocation strategy by monetizing value from high-quality, stabilized assets and redeploying that capital into grocery-anchored and everyday retail opportunities with strong growth potential," Phillips Edison Chief Executive Jeff Edison said.
The venture will be initially seeded with about half of the portfolio, with the rest of the assets expected to be transferred in stages by early 2027.
